text:
erica: Heads-up — saw a correctness regression in prefix eviction during tenant handoff on staging. When a lease moves we sometimes get duplicate residency & a short window of stale reads. Repro snippet below.

devin: ouch, can you paste the minimal repro/logs?

erica: pasted below:
```
I0321 12:01:23 handoff.go:217 AcquireLease tenant=acct-42 epoch=112
I0321 12:01:23 cache.go:412 EvictPrefix tenant=acct-42 prefix=abc shard=3
I0321 12:01:23 handoff.go:225 ReleaseLease tenant=acct-42 epoch=112
I0321 12:01:24 read.go:88 Read prefix=abc -> stale
```

erica: quick hypothesis: race between EvictPrefix and ReleaseLease where Evict marks slab free but doesn't clear the residency bit before handoff finishes. So a new owner can briefly see an entry that points to freed slab.

sam: is this related to the prefetch/admission-control refactor we landed last week? I remember a fast-path that skips tombstone on demote.

devin: could be. On demote fast-path we avoid the tombstone write to save latency — that could leave a ghost entry if handoff interleaves.

joan: short-term fix idea: add an explicit handoff_in_progress flag on the prefix object and make eviction bail out while flag is set. Cheap and conservative.

erica: implementation sketch:
```
func TryEvict(p *Prefix) bool {
  if p.handoffFlag {
    return false
  }
  if atomic.LoadInt32(&p.residencyCount) == 0 {
    p.markEvicted() // safe because handoffFlag false
    return true
  }
  return false
}
```

devin: that avoids the stale-read window but I'm worried about starving eviction under heavy handoff churn. Could cause memory pressure.

sam: what about using ephemeral sequence tokens for handoff ownership? token ensures only one actor can perform demote/evict for a prefix at a time; eviction requires token ownership + epoch check. Lighter than global flags.

erica: yeah seq tokens + epoch-compare sounds promising: owner obtains token, does demote/clear, then releases. Evict checks token==0 or token==ours.

joan: design note: make token acquisition cheap and lock-free (CAS on header). Also expose metrics: handoff_token_acquire_failures, blocked_evictions, stale_read_count.

devin: agree on metrics. Also add a short canary: enable seq-token guard in staging for a subset of shards and run churny tenant simulation for 30m.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: staging-kv -> feature/seq-token-guard canary at 09:30 PDT (rollout 10% shards).

erica: I'll open a mini-RFC / PR with the opt-in flag, metrics spec, and the staging canary test plan. Ping @devin @sam @joan for review.

devin: :thumbsup:

sam: :eyes:

erica: TL;DR — short-term: opt-in handoff token (sequence token) to serialize demote+evict; long-term: consider compact atomic ops in runtime to co-update lease/residency atomically.
